biological.citation: Store-operated calcium entry is reduced in spastin-linked hereditary spastic paraplegia (PMID: 36103408)
biological.summary: Loss of spastin enlarges the ER and reduces store-operated calcium entry (SOCE). Elevated spastin variants cluster STIM1 in the ER and impair its transport to the plasma membrane. SPAST-HSP patient iPSC-derived neurons show reduced SOCE and axonal swellings, and CRISPR/Cas9 correction of the SPAST variants rescues both.

biological.citation: Conserved pharmacological rescue of hereditary spastic paraplegia-related phenotypes across model organisms (PMID: 26744324)
biological.summary: Null SPAST homologues in C. elegans, Drosophila and zebrafish show locomotor defects linked to ER stress. These defects were partially rescued by phenazine, methylene blue, N-acetyl-cysteine, guanabenz and salubrinal, and ER stress biomarkers correlated with the improvement.

biological.citation: Spastin binds to lipid droplets and affects lipid metabolism (PMID: 25875445)
biological.summary: Spastin-M1 sorts from the ER to lipid droplets via a hydrophobic motif (aa 57-86, with R65 required). It acts as a conserved positive regulator of lipid droplet metabolism. Dspastin overexpression or knockdown in Drosophila, and spas-1 depletion in C. elegans, altered lipid droplet number and size, triacylglycerol levels and fat stores.

biological.citation: Hereditary spastic paraplegia: gain-of-function mechanisms revealed by new transgenic mouse (PMID: 30520996)
biological.summary: SPAST-C448Y transgenic mice expressing human mutant spastin show adult-onset gait defects and dying-back of corticospinal axons without haploinsufficiency. The mutant alters microtubule stability opposite to haploinsufficiency predictions. Cultured neurons show organelle transport deficits that are worsened by depletion of endogenous spastin, supporting a gain-of-function mechanism.

biological.citation: Modeling gain-of-function and loss-of-function components of SPAST-based hereditary spastic paraplegia using transgenic mice (PMID: 34935948)
biological.summary: Crossing Spast-KO mice with hSPAST-C448Y mice produced axonal swellings, earlier onset, worse gait deficits and more corticospinal dieback than C448Y alone. Changes in HDAC6 and tubulin modifications were also seen in the axon. Loss of function exacerbates mutant toxicity.

biological.citation: Spastin MIT Domain Disease-Associated Mutations Disrupt Lysosomal Function (PMID: 31787869)
biological.summary: Three disease-associated MIT-domain spastin mutants failed to promote endosomal tubule fission, lysosomal enzyme receptor trafficking or normal lysosomal morphology. One mutant impaired recruitment to endosomes, which depends on MIT binding to ESCRT-III proteins. The others did not, suggesting non-canonical MIT roles. Microtubule-severing capacity was unaffected.

biological.citation: Missense mutation of SPAST protein (I344K) results in loss of ATPase activity and prolonged the half-life (PMID: 30006150)
biological.summary: I344K-SPAST has defective ATPase and microtubule-severing activity but a prolonged protein half-life through altered post-translational modification for proteasomal degradation. It causes microtubule accumulation and inhibits neurite growth in neuroblastoma, neural progenitor cells and mouse cortical neurons. Wild-type M1 SPAST interacts with the mutant and reduces these effects dose-dependently.

biological.citation: Alu-mediated SPAST deletion impairs golgi zinc transport and reveals a druggable vulnerability (PMID: 42521669)
biological.summary: An Alu-mediated SPAST exon 17 deletion in hPSC-derived cortical organoids and xenografts creates SPAST-SLC30A6 fusion transcripts and reduces ZnT6 expression. This causes cytosolic zinc accumulation, Golgi fragmentation and Aβ/ubiquitin aggregation. TPEN or a GRASP55-blocking antibody rescued Golgi integrity and reduced Aβ.

biological.citation: CRISPR activation to characterize splice-altering variants in easily accessible cells (PMID: 38272032)
biological.summary: SPAST is predominantly expressed in the CNS and is not readily expressed in skin fibroblasts. dCas9-VPR CRISPRa strongly upregulated SPAST transcription in fibroblasts, enabling profiling of splice-altering variants by RT-PCR, NGS and long-read sequencing.

biological.citation: A novel truncated variant in SPAST results in spastin accumulation and defects in microtubule dynamics (PMID: 38066582)
biological.summary: The frameshift variant c.483_484delinsC (p.Val162Leufs*2) produced truncated M1 and M87 mutants that accumulated at higher levels with increased stability and likely lost microtubule-severing activity. This suggests toxic accumulation rather than pure haploinsufficiency in a five-generation family.
